title: openai-invoke-affinity-annotations-and-fragment-serializer
author: Maya Park
description: Motivation: Improve OpenAI-compat tool/function-call selection by exposing an 'invoke_affinity' annotation on tool metadata and by making streaming fragments self-descriptive so tool calls are never mis-routed or partially applied by downstream coalescers. Summary: 1) Add a non-breaking 'invoke_affinity' optional annotation to the tool registry and mapper (values: high|normal|low|prefer_local) that is used by the OpenAI-compat selection heuristic to bias tool_choice without hard overrides. 2) Serialize tool invocation fragments emitted during streaming with a compact header (v1) containing id, affinity, and schema-hash so fragment coalescers and proxies can re-assemble or route fragments deterministically. 3) Update the compatibility layer to treat tool messages with affinity=high as preferred targets for low-latency lanes (dedicated pools) and affinity=prefer_local to prefer the caller's region. 4) Ensure backwards compatibility: missing invoke_affinity behaves the same as 'normal' and fragment header is optional but validated when present. Checklist: - [x] design doc + API sketch included in PR description - [x] runtime mapper + serializer implementation - [x] unit + integration tests for selection weighting and streaming reassembly - [x] docs and SDK TS surface updates - [x] migration notes and rollout plan - [x] perf microbench showing ~0.9x selector CPU and no additional p99 token latency Changes are scoped so the OpenAI-compat surface preserves the existing function calling contract while giving product teams a low-risk knob to bias routing for latency/cost. See linked Linear tickets and end-to-end test results. Migration: rollout via feature flag 'openai.invoke_affinity' for 2 weeks, collect telemetry; revert safe if any metric regressions >5% on request success or latency. Backwards compatibility: older proxies that ignore the fragment header will still receive integrity-protected JSON tool payloads; routers that see affinity will incorporate it into their weighted selection but will not change function signatures. Related: this complements the 'stream-fragment-tagging' work but focuses on tool selection semantics rather than coalescing heuristics.

b3e4f5a: implement compact fragment header serializer/deserializer
c6d7e8b: integrate affinity into openai compatibility selection heuristic
d9f0a1b: add unit tests for weighting and header roundtrip
e2f3a4c: docs: describe invoke_affinity and migration plan
f5b6c7d: sdk(ts): surface affinity on ToolDescriptor and examples
diff_snippets:
services/openai-compat/src/tool_mapper.rs: +pub enum InvokeAffinity { High, Normal, Low, PreferLocal }
+impl Default for InvokeAffinity { fn default() -> Self { InvokeAffinity::Normal } }

services/serving/runtime/stream_serializer.rs: +// v1 header: 1 byte version | 1 byte flags | 16 byte tool-id | var affinity-tag | 4 byte schema-hash
+fn write_fragment_header(w: &mut impl Write, hdr: &FragmentHeader) -> io::Result<()> { /* compact encoding */ }

sdk/typescript/src/tool_descriptor.ts: +export type InvokeAffinity = 'high' | 'normal' | 'low' | 'prefer_local'
+export interface ToolDescriptor { id: string; name: string; invokeAffinity?: InvokeAffinity }
review_comments: Ethan Liu: Quick note — why are we using 'prefer_local' instead of a region tag? Can we expand the enum later without schema churn?

Maya Park (author): We chose 'prefer_local' as a lightweight hint; it's intentionally orthogonal to explicit region tags so schedulers can use both. We'll document extension rules in the compatibility doc.
Priya Natarajan: Integration test failed once on flaky network emulation, re-run CI after addressing stream backpressure edge-case.
Maya Park (author): Fixed backpressure by deferring header emission until first non-empty fragment; re-ran tests and added a stress case.
release_notes: Introduce optional invoke_affinity annotation for tool metadata and a streaming fragment header v1 to improve deterministic routing and avoid partial tool-call application during streaming. Backwards compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
notes: Rollout plan: enable flag on 10% of traffic for 48h, inspect selector-weighted telemetry, then 100% if no regressions. SDKs publish minor bump. Ops: update routing policy to read affinity hints but ensure cost guardrails are enforced.
